Chelsea said Wednesday night that Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter has agreed to sell his minority stake in the club to Clearlake Capital.

Clearlake, which already held a 61.5% stake in the club, is also acquiring the stake of Chelsea Chairman Todd Boehly, giving it full control of the storied club, according to Chelsea. Boehly and Walter each held about 12.8% of the club.
Boehly, who is a co-owner of the Dodgers, and Walter each held about 12.8% of the club.

The Financial Times reported that the two men will receive a combined £950 million, or $1.27 billion, for their stakes in the deal, which values Chelsea at £5 billion. Boehly is departing as the club’s chairman.
The Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss “will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group,” the club’s statement said.
The sale comes more than a month after the announcement that Walter had agreed to sell his controlling ownership
in the Los Angeles Lakers to Joshua Kushner and former Disney (DIS) CEO Bob Iger.

title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter to sell minority stake in Chelsea to Clearlake
